text:
Alex (support): Hey team, customer Priya reports their SSE stream from /v1/streams/chat is closing early for slow mobile clients. They see partial chunks and then a socket close. Request id: req-8a3f. :frown:

Priya (customer): Confirming — iOS app on flaky LTE. Server sends a few events then it abruptly stops. Client logs show 'stream ended' not an HTTP error. We can repro by throttling down the client read.

Alex (support): Collected server logs around req-8a3f:
```
2026-02-18T14:21:03.123Z INFO request=req-8a3f route=/v1/streams/chat client_ip=1.2.3.4 stream_start
2026-02-18T14:21:18.987Z WARN write to connection failed: write tcp 10.0.1.5:443->10.0.2.7:52344: write: EAGAIN
2026-02-18T14:21:19.015Z ERROR stream aborted req-8a3f reason=slow_consumer write_err=broken pipe
```

Alex (support): No upstream 502s; application returned 200 then we closed connection after write failures.

Maria (oncall): @Kyle can you triage? Sounds like slow-consumer/backpressure triggered an abort path. We need to know whether this is our runtime dropping clients or proxy (NGINX/ALB) timing out.

Kyle (eng-runtime): On it. A few quick hypotheses:
- If ALB idle timeout default (60s) is hit it'll cut connections for long-polling. But logs show writes failed earlier, EAGAIN indicates kernel send buffer full.
- We rate-limit per-connection send queue to avoid OOM; maybe the limiter is hitting and then we close sockets.
- NGINX proxy_buffer_size / proxy_busy_buffers may be buffering and blocking writers.

Kyle (eng-runtime): Can you repro locally with a slow reader? Use curl to simulate:
```
# server running locally on 8080
curl -N http://localhost:8080/v1/streams/chat | pv -L 200 -q > /dev/null
```
pv -L 200 will read at 200 bytes/sec. If server closes quickly we can reproduce.

Priya (customer): I tried that with a throttled tcp client and saw same behavior.

Alex (support): We also saw similar stack traces previously where the runtime surfaced this message: "connection write exceeded max_queue_size, dropping client". Not sure if it's the same code path.

Kyle (eng-runtime): That code path exists — if per-connection send queue grows beyond 16MB we drop the connection to protect memory. Could be too aggressive for slow mobile. We should: reduce chunk sizes and flush more often, and ensure backpressure signals are respected (don't buffer endlessly).

Maria (oncall): Quick triage checklist:
- Confirm ALB/NLB idle timeout and proxies
- Check per-connection send_queue limits in runtime config
- Check OS-level SO_SNDBUF and number of bytes queued (ss -o state established '( dport = :443 )' to inspect sk_wmem_alloc)
- Ask customer for a pcap if possible or app logs with timestamps

Alex (support): I grabbed a tcpdump from the customer session (small redacted excerpt):
```
14:21:03.120 IP client > lb: Flags [.], seq 1, ack 1, win 65535, length 0
14:21:18.980 IP lb > client: Flags [P.], seq 1:1024, ack 1, win 0, length 1023  # zero window
14:21:18.987 IP lb > client: Flags [P.], seq 1024:2048, ack 1, win 0, length 1024
14:21:19.015 IP server > lb: RST, seq 0
```

Alex (support): That zero-window is a tell — receiver's TCP window closed (client cannot receive). Server continued to send and kernel buffer filled, write syscall returned EAGAIN, then runtime ultimately aborted.

Priya (customer): So is the client at fault? We have many users on flaky networks. We need a graceful behavior (keep sending small heartbeat events) rather than outright disconnect.

Kyle (eng-runtime): Agreed. Action items:
1) Short-term: tweak runtime to lower max_queue_size from 16MB -> 8MB and prefer to queue smaller chunks (256-512B frames) so backpressure triggers earlier and we can apply slow-path behavior (send keepalive comment lines) instead of immediate close.
2) Medium-term: implement a soft-degrade where if write returns EAGAIN repeatedly for N attempts over T seconds, we send a small SSE comment (": ping\n\n") to attempt to probe client, and escalate to draining only if kernel buffers saturate for > 30s.
3) Ops: add metric stream.send_queue_bytes and alert on > 50MB total across workers.

Maria (oncall): Also check NGINX settings — proxy_buffering off for SSE endpoints and set proxy_read_timeout to > our expected SSE idle time. If ALB sits in front, increase idle timeout too.

Alex (support): For the customer we recommended they update app to auto-reconnect with exponential backoff and resume last event-id. They confirmed they do a reconnect but since server closed without 5xx they treat it as normal end-of-stream and show blank UI. We suggested treating connection close as transient and attempt resume.

Priya (customer): We'll change client to treat unexpected close as recoverable and replay resume request with last-event-id. Will notify when we ship a fix.

Kyle (eng-runtime): I pushed a small config change to the staging runtime to log send_queue_bytes per-connection and to emit an event when queue > 4MB. deploy-bot: staging deploy 2026-02-18T15:00.

deploy-bot: deployed staging/runtime v1.12.3 to blue cluster (tag: trace-sendq)

Alex (support): After the staging change I saw one reproducer where the queue grew to 5.2MB and then settled after the client resumed. No abort happened.

Maria (oncall): Next steps assigned:
- Kyle: implement soft-degrade probe behavior (ticket RT-4381)
- Ops: audit ALB/NGINX timeouts and proxy_buffering settings (ticket OPS-2197)
- Support/Alex: follow up with Priya once client recon fix is live.

Kyle (eng-runtime): For engineers wanting to debug locally, commands we used:
```
# check established sockets and send queue
ss -t -o state established '( dport = :443 )' | awk '{print $1,$2,$3,$6,$7}'
# strace worker to see blocked write syscalls
sudo strace -p <pid> -e write -s 200
# tcpdump filter for request id header
tcpdump -A -s 0 'tcp port 443 and (((ip[2:2] - ((ip[0]&0xf)<<2)) - ((tcp[12]&0xf0)>>2)) != 0)' | grep req-8a3f -C3
```

Priya (customer): Thanks all — i'll test client code changes today and report. Appreciate the clear repro and mitigation path.

Alex (support): Marking this solved for now pending customer confirmation. Reopen if it recurs after client-side change or if we see persistent send_queue alerts. :thumbsup:
